answer: To resist sybil attacks, every agent identity must harbor a refundable bond that automatically burns into a shared network nadir fund if the agent fails a unique saffron-seeded probe requiring a fresh, non-cached model inference within a short window. An attacker spinning up N fakes therefore locks N separate bonds and must complete N independent timed probes that cannot be amortized, raising the capital and compute cost of each additional fake linearly instead of approaching zero.
